questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are crossing.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign means you are near a school. Watch for children and stop if they are crossing.

questions.question: When should you shift gears in a curve?

options.text: Only if you can do it smoothly.
It is better than shifting before the curve.
It is the best way to control speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you can do it smoothly.
questions.explanation: Shift gears before turning whenever possible. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change can make the rear wheel skid.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is near the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before riding.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, what may you need to do?

options.text: Slow down with your brakes before shifting to a lower gear.
Speed up before shifting to a lower gear.
Flash your brakes to alert drivers behind you that you are downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down with your brakes before shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed before shifting to a lower gear. Downshifting while going too fast can cause the motorcycle to lurch and the rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down at a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: When should you do head checks?

options.text: Rarely, because they take your eyes off the road.
Often as part of your normal routine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often as part of your normal routine.
questions.explanation: Check around you frequently. Knowing what is happening around you helps you be ready for anything.

questions.question: As your weight moves forward during braking, what can you do?

options.text: Use less pressure on the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: As your weight shifts forward while braking, the front wheel has more grip. You can use more front brake pressure.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid injury on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on slippery surfaces. Sudden movements on slippery roads can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you always avoid?

options.text: No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best or always bad. Choose a position that fits your riding conditions.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull the clutch?

options.text: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
You start to lose control in a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, use the engine cut-off switch and pull the clutch right away. This removes power from the rear wheel so you can safely stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop and look both ways before going.
Let other traffic go first before you enter or cross.
Keep going at the same speed and check all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic go first before you enter or cross.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and be ready to stop. Let any car, bike rider, or pedestrian pass before you go. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is joining from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is joining from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic will be entering the road from the right side.

questions.question: Keep enough space behind other vehicles:

options.text: So you have time to see dangers and react to them.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
So other drivers will cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you have time to see dangers and react to them.
questions.explanation: Space between you and the car ahead gives you room to stop or move if that car stops suddenly. It also helps you see problems on the road, like potholes.

questions.question: Use more space between you and other vehicles:

options.text: When the road is wet or icy.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is wet or icy.
questions.explanation: A two-second gap is normal. Use a bigger gap when the road is icy or wet. These conditions make it harder to stop.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look where you want to go through the turn. Turn your head but not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level.

questions.question: What affects a person's blood alcohol level (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: How much alcohol they drink
questions.explanation: Three things affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the person's body weight.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you from behind, stay:

options.text: On the shoulder of the road.
On the left side of your lane.
In the middle of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: The middle of the lane is safest when being passed. Riding close to the passing car risks a crash. Riding far from it might make the driver return too soon.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, you should NOT:

options.text: Give them other things to do to slow their drinking.
Keep them from leaving until they are sober.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Never let an impaired person ride. Instead, get them a safe ride home, find other activities to do, keep them from leaving until sober, and ask other friends to help stop them.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are divided by:
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same way. A solid white line means do not pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Check your motorcycle before riding:
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always check your motorcycle before each ride. Small problems are more dangerous on a motorcycle than in a car.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the right portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
As close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Without signaling so you don't distract the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing. Signal before you pass, check for traffic, and return to your original lane when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass you.
questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass you. If you speed up, they may tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of a lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: An oily or greasy strip
questions.explanation: Oil and grease from cars build up in the center of lanes. Unless the road is wet, it is usually still safe for a motorcycle to ride there.

questions.question: Why should you ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass?

options.text: It gives you a better view ahead.
It makes it hard to see the vehicle you are passing.
It helps the other driver speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a better view ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to see further ahead and to be more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign means there is a railroad crossing ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on slippery surfaces. Use both brakes when stopping and avoid making sudden movements.

questions.question: If you are preparing to pass another rider on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the right part of the lane so they see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center part of the lane so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to see further ahead and to be more visible to drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: When do you NOT need a larger cushion of space between you and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.
When weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: When weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in bad weather, when roads are slippery, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When slowing down or stopping, what must you do with the gears?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a tire go flat. Tire failure usually shows up as a sudden change in how the motorcycle handles.
